title: The Critical Rendering Path: Why It Matters

scenes.line1: Why do some pages load instantly?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why some web pages pop up fast, while others crawl? Let’s break down the critical rendering path—the browser’s roadmap for turning code into pixels.
The browser takes these steps: parses HTML and CSS, builds the DOM and CSSOM, combines them into a render tree, lays out elements, and finally paints pixels.
Changing layout triggers a reflow, which is costly. Repaint just updates pixels—much cheaper. Avoid unnecessary reflows for speed.

scenes.label: Vitals
scenes.sub: LCP, INP, and CLS measure real user experience.
scenes.say: Core Web Vitals—Largest Contentful Paint, Interaction to Next Paint, and Cumulative Layout Shift—track how fast and stable your site feels to users.

scenes.question: Does bundle size affect rendering?
scenes.right: Yes, smaller bundles mean less code to parse and faster rendering.
scenes.say: Here’s a common interview trap: Does bundle size affect rendering? It absolutely does. Smaller bundles mean less code to parse and quicker rendering.
